note: Adversarial held-out candidates for German segment.inConstituents and segment.inMorphemes, drafted 2026-10-29 as Draft Breakdown Records in records/breakdown/de to judge round 8 (#1241). Reported apart from the headline real-text set (breakdown-heldout-2026-10-29-realtext): fresh words on both sides of each round-8 fix, so the score says whether a fix generalizes or overreaches, not whether its tuning cases pass. Per row: AD1 Nachwelt, AD2 Zuname and AD3 Beiname, a noun whose first part DWDS's Wortzerlegung links to the preposition (1nach, 1zu, 1bei), so outside a verb the particle-like part links to its ADP (ADR 0054), against AD4 nachfragen, where the same particle inside a verb keeps its Prefix nach- (class D1); AD5 bezahlen and AD6 erleben, a prefix and a base verb whose letters also offer the prefix, a noun (Zahl, Leben) and the citation ending, against AD7 verkörpern, ver- + Körper + n, where no verb körpern exists, so the noun reading must stay (class D2); AD8 salzig and AD9 staubig, an -ig base that is a noun (Salz, Staub) and a verb's stem (salzen, stauben) but no adjective, against AD10 rutschig, whose base is the verb rutschen though Rutsch is a noun too (class D3). Every word split follows the DWDS Wortzerlegung (ADR 0054), cited in its record. Avoided: every Lemma with a Breakdown Record; the real-text batch's Lemmas; the words the round-8 unit tests use (Umweg, umfahren, Hinweg, versalzen, verbrennen, durstig); words a Breakdown prompt names; ADR 0054's own examples (Ausland); Mitmensch and überall, whose DWDS links (the prefix mit-, 2über) would contest the ADP rule; Sources. Consistency sets: D1 a particle outside a verb against inside one; D2 prefix + verb against prefix + noun + ending; D3 an -ig base's noun against its verb. Judged 2026-10-29 by two independent judges, system and learner POV (#1241): both keep all ten rows as drafted. They stay out of every Breakdown prompt's examples (#693).
